item.title: Don Mikkelsen Quartet — Sat Aug 15, 8:00 PM — Hotel Eve Jazz
item.description: Don Mikkelsen has played trombone professionally for over 50 years, performing internationally with artists such as Frank Sinatra, Tony Bennett, Blood Sweat & Tears, Nancy Wilson, Sammy Davis Jr., Marvin Gaye, Elvis Presley, Peggy Lee, and Michel Legrand, and on recordings of such diverse artists as Louie Bellson, Grand Master Flash, and Peter Gabriel (Sledgehammer). More recently, he appears on Tony Levin’s 2024 album ‘Bringing It Down to the Bass’. Don counts among his influences Louis Armstrong, Lester Young, Stan Getz, and many others, of course including trombone heroes J.J. Johnson and Jack Teagarden, and is inspired to preserve and share the tradition of classic swinging jazz. Featuring: Taylor Pierson (Piano) Steve LaSpina (Bass) Rick Dilling (Drums) $10 weekdays -$15 weekends at the door (all ticket proceeds are 100% passed to the band, backed by a living wage guarantee from Hotel Eve) *Reserve a table in advance, or join us impromptu the night of the show. item.title: AT - Spivey Gap to Little Bald, Out and Back FITNESS Hike — Wed Aug 19, 9:00 AM
item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group We will start at the AT parking area on 19W which is just past where the AT crosses the road.
It is approximately 9.5 miles out and back with about 2900' of elevation gain. There are quite a few steep sections to climb on this route. We will take a short side trail to the top of High Rock on the way. Little Bald isn't really a bald. there is a view point on a rock where we can stop for lunch. I scouted this hike a couple of weeks ago. The trail is in good shape but be prepared to see a lot of devastated trees in parts of the hike. The weather is supposed to be warm and sunny on Weds. High of 77 at The gap. Any rain cancellation will be made by 7:00 am.
If you want to carpool, meet at the Park and Ride at Exit 17 on I-26 west at 8:10. Please let me know if you plan to carpool or meet at the trailhead.

item.title: Laurel Creek Hike — Fri Aug 21, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Asheville Mountains-to-Sea Trail Hiking Club 2.0 PLEASE MAKE SURE TO FOLLOW THE DIRECTIONS ABOUT WHERE WE MEET AND DO NOT DEPEND UPON GPS. AS YOU ARE DRIVING TOWARD HOT SPRINGS, YOU WILL GO DOWN A FAIRLY STEEP GRADE AND THERE WILL BE A BIG PARKING LOT ON THE LEFT BEFORE THE LEFT TURN TO GO TO HOT SPRINGS. THIS IS WHERE WE MEET.
We'll meet at the trailhead parking area right off the road to Hot Springs at 8:50 and plan to leave the parking area no later than 9 a.m. We'll walk in and out, approximate 7 miles RT. We hike at a good pace (about 2.7 per hour) with one break half way through. Well behaved dogs allowed. Bring a snack or lunch. We'll stop by the French Broad River 1/2 way through. We'll be finished with the hike around 11:30-noon.
Source: Asheville Mountains-to-Sea Trail Hiking Club

item.description:

This is a fairlly easy hike, and we go at a high average to low advanced speed, which is roughly about 3.0 to 3.2 mph. There are no super long hills. It's pretty undulating all the way. The biggest hill is at the beginning.

item.title: Hidden in Plain Sight — Thu Sep 3, 1:00 PM
item.description:
Hidden in Plain Sight with Eric Young Thursday, September 3 | 1 – 3pm BRN – Elective Register Here!
Wildlife plays tricks on each other to survive. Predators blend-in to surprise prey. The prey blends in to hide from predators. Not only will participants discover some of the best camouflaged animals in nature but they will also have their observation skills tested. There are many ways that nature hides wildlife, join naturalist/environmental educator, Eric Young, and come find out the many adaptations wildlife employs to stay alive. This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. Eric Young retired down to North Carolina in 2020 after 23 years as a program director at the nature center on Long island. item.title: Franklinia Tree Paper Flower Workshop — Fri Sep 4, 11:00 AM
item.description:
Franklinia Tree Paper Flower Workshop with Cynthia Woodsong Friday, September 4 | 11am – 4pm Register Here!
Join naturalist Cynthia Woodsong in this informative and hands-on workshop learning how to create botanically accurate paper flowers and leaves of the unique Franklinia alatamaha, the beautiful and enigmatic shrub or small tree described by William Bartram in the late 18th century. This workshop starts by joining the Lunch & Learn program led by Jim Costa, which includes a talk and guided observation of the impressive specimen at the Arboretum. Following the talk, workshop participants will use their new knowledge to help guide them in creating paper flowers and leaves on an actual Franklinia branch under Cynthia’s direction. All materials are provided. Cynthia Woodsong is a North Carolina Master Naturalist with a certificate in Botanical Art and Illustration from the North Carolina Botanical Garden, UNC Chapel Hill. item.title: Ledford Branch Loop: 5 mi., 500 ft. Elev. Gain — Fri Aug 21, 9:00 AM
item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group **[RSVP opens Sunday Aug. 16th, 8:00 pm]**
This is a typical lovely hike in the Bent Creek area. The route I've cobbled together adds up to about 5 miles and a relatively mild 500' elevation gain. With the hills and moderate pace -- around 2.5 mph -- I'd rate it 2.5 on a 0-10 difficulty scale. It's not a "fitness hike," but you'll need to be able to walk up and down some hilly terrain.
We'll traverse a mishmash of trail segments and connectors, from wide gravel roads to single-file trails, mostly good footing. Around halfway through we'll find a spot for a short snack break.
Wear sensible hiking footwear. Bring some water. If you're on the fence about hiking poles, you probably don't need them for this one.
***Dog Policy:*** Dogs are extremely welcome but must be leashed.
